label: San Francisco

county_election_office.name: San Francisco Department of Elections, City Hall, Room 48 (Voting Center open for early voting from Oct. 5)

zip_caveats: San Francisco is one city and one county, so every voter gets the same citywide races and measures. What a ZIP code can't tell you is your district races. Every SF ZIP overlaps two or more Supervisor districts (DataSF crosswalk, 2022 lines), and only even-numbered districts (2, 4, 6, 8, 10) elect a supervisor this year; if you live in District 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 or 11 you have no supervisor race. Your Congress district (11, or 15 in a small southern area), Assembly district (17 east, 19 west) and BART district (only District 8 votes this year) also depend on your exact address. Check your own sample ballot in the Voter Portal (sfelections.gov/voterportal) or the pamphlet mailed to you. A mailing address outside the city line, such as Daly City or Brisbane, gets a San Mateo County ballot instead.
